author: けりー
text:
I can't keep up with notebooks or planners either! Even if I buy an expensive notebook, I lose the desire to write in it halfway through, get demotivated by my messy handwriting, or end up straying from the original purpose and turning it into a chaotic mess that I hate—doesn't anyone else have perfectionist tendencies like that? That's me, but for people like that, here's the perfect notebook usage technique.

Buy a notebook that has page numbers and a table of contents list. And ignore rules like using it from the front—use it freely. Just write the page you wrote on and the content (topic level) into the table of contents. I start by numbering from 1 to 188 and write wherever I want. For example, 1. I write 8/1 and do that day's journaling, 56. travel plans, something like that, without writing from the front sequentially.

But even if you write haphazardly, you can look back on it later, and even if it's miscellaneous, you can manage it. This is inspired by bullet journal-style usage. Thanks to this, I no longer abandon expensive notebooks after only using 10 pages. And now I'm using more than 10 fixed notebooks with numbering and tables of contents. Give it a try!!!
